title: Digital financial inclusion and sustainable employment: Evidence from countries along the belt and road
technology: digital financial inclusion index (IDFI): ATMs, credit bureau coverage, domestic credit, non-bank credit, credit information depth, legal rights, digital payments (weight 0.155)
estimator: FE; FE+IV (internet penetration IV); system GMM; MG/AMG; threshold model

title: The linear and non-linear impacts of ICT on economic growth, of disaggregate income groups within SSA region
technology: ICT: fixed telephone lines, mobile phone subscriptions, internet subscriptions (per 100 inhabitants) and a fixed+mobile composite
estimator: Pooled Mean Group (PMG) panel ARDL/ECM; MG comparison; Pedroni cointegration

contrasts.outcome: GDP per capita (dependent variable, long-run PMG)
contrasts.estimator: Pooled Mean Group (PMG); MG reported as comparison
contrasts.evidence: Table 9 vs Table 7 (PMG col. 2; Section 4.4, journal pp. 561-563): FIX row, e.g. Table 9 fixed telephone lines 0.4168 (0.00)
contrasts.notes: Parentheses in Tables 7-9 are p-values (table note), so SE and t are null; N is read from the PMG column of the table N row (column order inferred, PMG columns = 2,4,6,8). Only the Hausman PMG-vs-MG test is reported, within each group; no cross-group difference test. Outcome is a benefit (higher GDP per capita is better). Groups: no high-income economies in the SSA sample, so richest = upper-middle; Table 9 is titled upper-middle but the text calls it higher-income (p.313-315). Headline chosen as mobile (MOB), the abstract's most robust ICT result; judgement call.
